rounds.name: Technical Interview – Round 1
rounds.description: My interview started with a basic introduction and he got very interested in asking about my startup that I worked on during my 2nd and 3rd year. Then he asked about my ml project that I have worked on in one of the hackathons.

questions.text: The deadline of a project is 2 weeks but tech team is not working efficiently what will you do??
Tell the number of users you can get of your turf booking app (my startup) in the first quarter in kolkata.
Why Quantiphi?

rounds.name: Technical Interview – Round 2
rounds.description: It was online and pretty chill. He started by asking my introduction and he was also interested in my startup work. Then he asked many questions related to python.

questions.text: Tell me what does quantiphi do and 3 projects

rounds.name: HR Round
rounds.description: It was not a typical hr round . many management case based questions and guesstimates were also asked.

questions.text: Where do you live and my family background?
How will you pitch our insurance automation tool to a law firm?
Guess number of ev vehicles in india.

tips.text: Always start the gd – I started the gd addressing the group clearly channelised the whole flow and told the topics that would be discussed.
Be confident and focus on your communication and presentation skills it matters a lot.
Research everything about the company what niche they work on, what projects are ongoing , their top services and products.
You should know your resume in and out and should be able to explain everything in it.
Many factors work except your performance so don’t overthink much just give your best , one day it will pay off and you are gonna get the offer.

rounds.name: FE Round 2

questions.text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL?
Why Quantiphi? Who are Quantiphi’s competitors?

rounds.name: HR Round
rounds.description: Management and stakeholder interview focusing on situational questions and project flaws without mentioning projects initially.

questions.text: If your team members are not working, how would you tackle them?
How would you convince stakeholders to buy your product?

You are linking each question to your project — what possible flaws can you detect in the project? If you knew them, what actions did you take to overcome them, and how would you still manage to retain consumers even after those problems?

tips.text: For serious prep, I would strongly recommend going through R.S. Aggarwal’s aptitude book, because companies are raising the bar year by year.
The interviewer was more interested in my projects because they had practical use cases and impact.
Be prepared for DSA and SQL — even if my round was light on these (just 10 minutes), that may not be the case for everyone.
Aptitude is the real filter. Many strong students were ruled out early, including me in 2–3 companies. The level of aptitude is rising every year.
For aptitude, prepare thoroughly from R.S. Aggarwal
Have a clear end-to-end understanding of your projects — the idea, use case, challenges, and solutions. Even if you’ve adapted a project from GitHub, know it in depth as if it’s your own.
Be thorough with every word in your resume. Some interviewers will focus heavily on projects, others may focus more on fundamentals or DSA . You need to be ready for both.

rounds.name: Online Assessment
rounds.description: The test was held on campus via Unstop with rigorous proctoring. It contained three sections – Aptitude, Technical MCQs, and Coding. Each section had a sectional timer.

questions.text: Minimum Robbing Speed – A thief wants to rob all the houses in a village. Given an array representing the number of houses in each neighborhood and the maximum amount of time (in hours) available, find the minimum speed (houses per hour) required to rob the entire village.
House Robber Problem – This was the classic House Robber problem from LeetCode, solvable using a standard Dynamic Programming approach.

Maximum Loot on Islands – Given an undirected graph of n islands, each with a loot value, and edges representing travel paths with travel times, a pirate can start from any island and visit each island at most once. The total loot is the sum of the visited islands’ values, while the total time is the sum of the travel times along the chosen path.The task was to find the maximum loot which can be solved by direct Dijkstra’s Algorithm.

rounds.name: Technical Interview – Round 1
rounds.description: The interview started with my introduction.Then the interviewer asked me about my Major Project focusing mainly on its real-world application .Next he asked me about my Internship project at TCS and asked me to explain it in detail which I have implemented using Google Cloud Platform.Then he asked me simple programming question of Checking whether a number is pallindrome or not. I have started with brute force approach and then explained the optimal one .He also asked me questions about the other projects mentioned in my resume, focusing mainly on how I implemented specific features and the reasoning behind them .Finally I asked the interviewer a question and the interview was concluded.

questions.text: Checking whether a number is pallindrome or not

rounds.name: Technical Interview – Round 2
rounds.description: This interview started with a self-introduction. Then, the interviewer asked me about my internship project. He further asked about the difference between SQL and NoSQL in DBMS, followed by a discussion on normalization. After that, he asked me to design a database schema for a company with users as students, employees, teachers, and staff. His main objective was to assess my understanding of storing data in a normalized form. Next, he asked me to write a SQL query on the schema I had designed, having GROUP BY and ORDER BY operations. After this, he asked about the difference between JWT and Cookies. He then moved on to Sockets and Polling concepts. Further, he asked some basic Python questions such as the difference between lists and tuples and how multiple inheritance works in Python. Finally, he asked me about my Major Project.

questions.text: Design a database schema for a company with users as students, employees, teachers, and staff.
Write a SQL query on the schema I had designed, having GROUP BY and ORDER BY operations.
What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL in DBMS?
What is the difference between JWT and Cookies?
Explain Sockets and Polling concepts.
What is the difference between lists and tuples and how multiple inheritance works in Python?

rounds.name: HR Round
rounds.description: The HR round began with my self-introduction, followed by questions about my family background and where I live. Then, the interviewer asked me to pitch one of my projects of my choice in one minute as if I were pitching it to an investor. He also asked about the challenges I faced while working on that project.Next, he moved on to behavioral questions and a guesstimate question.

questions.text: Pitch one of my projects of my choice in one minute as if I were pitching it to an investor.
What are the challenges I faced while working on that project?
If I assign you a project about which you have no prior knowledge, how would you approach it?
If you are assigned three tasks with tight deadlines, how would you prioritize and work on them?
Estimate the number of daily users on YouTube.
Why do you want to join Quantiphi and where do you see yourself in the next five years?

tips.text: Try to answer theoretical questions with real-life use cases or examples to demonstrate a deeper understanding of the topic
Stay Positive and Believe in Yourself : The placement process can be long and stressful.
Prepare Based on Company Patterns : Go through previous interview experiences for the company you’re targeting.
Know Your Resume Inside Out : Be prepared for questions like “Why did you build this project?” or “How would you improve it further?”.
Cover Both DSA and Fundamentals : Don’t limit yourself to DSA alone. Computer fundamentals like OS, DBMS, OOPS, and Networks are equally important.
Stay Calm During Interviews: Interviews can be nerve-wracking. Practice mock interviews with friends or seniors.
Trust the Process and Don’t Compare : Trust God’s plan and your own journey. Failures are an unavoidable part of growth.

rounds.name: OA
rounds.description: We had 3 sections: Aptitude, Logical & Verbal Reasoning, CS Fundamentals, and Coding Problems.

questions.text: A thief wants to rob all the houses in a village. There is an array of the number of houses in each neighbourhood and the maximum amount of time(hours) he can take. At what minimum speed in houses per hour does he need to rob to clean the entire village?
A question very similar to the House Robber Problem from Leetcode. It was a basic include-exclude DP problem with one if condition.

You are given an undirected graph of n islands, each with a loot value, and edges representing travel paths between islands with their travel times. A pirate may start from any island, traveling along available paths, and can visit each island at most once. The total loot is the sum of the visited islands' values, while the total time is the sum of the travel times along the chosen path. Find the maximum loot the pirate can collect.

rounds.name: HR Interview
rounds.description: Typical HR interview enquiring about the candidate.

tips.text: Attempt the first section in multiple iterations, solving the easiest questions in the first one, then the next and so on. Time is a huge constraint here so manage it well.

DSA is extremely important but I feel like the amount of proficiency needed there is oversold. Having completed a popular problem roadmap like Strivers' SDE or Neetcode 150 will take you pretty far too.
Try to balance out your prep: Try to allocate your time wisely and try to revise CS Fundamentals and Projects alongside DSA.
Little buffs are fine but don’t lie and don’t write things you can’t explain in your resume.
Read Interview Experiences: You'll get to know how important which topic is for which company.
If you’re interested in ML, try your best to work on projects and learn as much as possible. But don’t depend on college for a placement in ML. Keep trying off campus too!
Always stay calm: Never argue with the interviewer to defend your points. Always stay calm.
Rejections: They are a part of life and you’ll face them from time to time. Don’t get disheartened.
